## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from OUP publisher pages and domain knowledge of social cognitive affective neuroscience editorial culture (SANS). Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | High |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Low-Medium — paradigm-unified neuroscience |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — cultural neuroscience, intersectional brain research |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Social-affective neuroscience — social cognition neural correlates, emotion regulation, theory of mind, empathy, moral neuroscience, neuroeconomics, cultural neuroscience |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **brain-behavior contribution at social-cognitive-affective intersection**. Neuroimaging / psychophysiology methodology expected.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Pure social psychology without neural measurement redirected; pure cognitive neuroscience without social-affective also redirected.

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Manuscripts without neural measurement
- AI use without disclosure per OUP policy
- Pure cognitive neuroscience without social-affective dimension

### Soft Tax

Low for SANS tradition authors. OA available via OUP.

### Best Suited For

- fMRI / EEG studies of social cognition
- Empathy and theory of mind neural research
- Emotion regulation neural mechanisms
- Moral neuroscience
- Neuroeconomics
- Cultural neuroscience
- Neuroimaging meta-analyses on social-affective topics

### Not Recommended For

- Pure social psychology behavioral work (consider JPSP, PSPB)
- Pure cognitive neuroscience without social-affective (consider JoCN)
- Pure clinical neuropsychology (consider Neuropsychology)

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience](../cognitive-science/journal-of-cognitive-neuroscience.md) | MIT Press; broader cognitive-neuroscience |
| 2 | [Neuropsychology](../cognitive-science/neuropsychology.md) | If clinical-population focused; APA |
| 3 | *(Cerebral Cortex / NeuroImage — community contribution welcome)* | Broader neuroscience venues |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from JoCN as "too social-affective," SCAN is the OUP SANS-affiliated home.
